messages.task:
You are a financial-analysis assistant that can solve quantitative questions by invoking Python tools.
When you need factual numbers (share prices, dates, etc.) call one of the tools that are provided to you.  Do not guess any value that can be obtained through a tool.  After finding the needed information, think exactly and output ONLY the final numeric answer in the requested format – nothing else.

Scenario excerpt (table with numbers intentionally omitted):
part ii item 5.
Market for registrant’s common equity, related stockholder matters and issuer purchases of equity securities. The following table presents reported quarterly high and low per-share sale prices of our Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) for the years 2006 and 2005.  [table omitted]
On February 22, 2007, the closing price of our Class A common stock was reported on the NYSE.
As of February 22, 2007, we had 419,988,395 outstanding shares of Class A common stock and 623 registered holders.
In February 2004, all outstanding shares of our Class B common stock were converted into shares of our Class A common stock on a one-for-one basis pursuant to the occurrence of the “dodge conversion event” as defined in our charter.  Also in February 2004, all outstanding shares of Class C common stock were converted into shares of Class A common stock on a one-for-one basis.  In August 2005, we amended and restated our charter to, among other things, eliminate our Class B common stock and Class C common stock.
Dividends – We have never paid a dividend on any class of our common stock.  We anticipate that we may retain future earnings, if any, to fund the development and growth of our business.  (Additional liquidity and covenant discussion omitted.)

Available tools (call them exactly as shown):
• lookup_quarter(year: int, quarter_label: str) -> dict
  Get the database row for the specified calendar quarter.
• fetch_price_for_quarter(quarter_id: int, share_class_symbol: str, stat: str = "high"|"low") -> float
  Retrieve the high or low share price for the given quarter and share class.
• fetch_daily_closing_price(trade_date: str|date, share_class_symbol: str) -> float
  Return the closing share price for a specific date and share class.
• calculate_percentage_growth(initial_price: float, final_price: float, precision: int = 1) -> float
  Compute percentage growth from one price to another.
• calculate_absolute_change(initial_price: float, final_price: float) -> float
  Compute the absolute change between two prices.

Question:
What is the growth rate in the price of shares from the highest value during the quarter ended December 31, 2006 and the closing price on February 22, 2007?
